title: Unity
summary: Notes for using Game Arts files in Unity. Written from the manual pages read on 2026-10-24 (Unity 6000.6); nothing was run in the editor, so every mapping is documented and none is observed.

import_guidance.text: Import the runtime copy as a Sprite (2D and UI) texture with Sprite Mode Multiple, then slice with Grid By Cell Size using the atlas cell size.
Set the texture's Filter Mode to Point (no filter).
Use Bilinear (or Trilinear with mipmaps) so the texture is not blocky up close.
Drag the borders in the Sprite Editor or type them in, set Mesh Type to Full Rect, and set the Sprite Renderer's Draw Mode to Sliced.

concept_map.engine_term: Sprite Mode Multiple, sliced in the Sprite Editor with Grid By Cell Size
concept_map.note: Equal cells only, so a grid sheet. Automatic slicing is based on the texture's transparency and does not follow the cells, so do not use it for these sheets.

concept_map.engine_term: the sprite's Pivot, where its local coordinate system originates
concept_map.note: Set it from the atlas pivot. The pages read do not state the pivot's units or origin corner.

concept_map.engine_term: Sprite Editor borders (the L, R, T and B fields) with the Sprite Renderer's Draw Mode set to Sliced
concept_map.note: The order of the editor fields (left, right, top, bottom) differs from the framework's [left, top, right, bottom]. Set Mesh Type to Full Rect: with Tight, 9-slicing might not work correctly.
The texture appears blocky up close.
The texture appears blurry up close; Trilinear also blends between mipmap levels.

concept_map.engine_term: a texture with alpha; Alpha Is Transparency dilates the colour channels
concept_map.note: The importer fills the colour under transparent pixels itself when that option is on, so the framework's runtime copies are not bled.
